segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Thanks for joining, today I want to walk through the updated dashboard redesign before we hand it to engineering for estimation.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Excited for this one, the current dashboard layout has been the same for almost two years.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Same, I've heard complaints from support about the sidebar navigation specifically, people say it's cluttered.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: That's exactly what this addresses. So starting from the top, we're moving from the left sidebar with twelve items down to a collapsible sidebar with five top level sections, and everything else lives inside those.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: Five sections, what are they?

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Overview, Funnels, Cohorts, Alerts, and Settings. Reports actually gets folded into Overview since usage data showed most people check reports right after landing on the dashboard anyway.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: That matches the usage data I pulled too, Reports as a standalone tab had really low direct navigation.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: How much of this is purely visual versus structural? Asking because structural changes touch more of our routing code.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: It's mostly structural honestly, we're not just reskinning, we're changing the information architecture. The good news is the underlying data calls don't change, just how they're organized on screen.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: That's a relief, I was worried this meant new API endpoints.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: No new endpoints needed for phase one. Let me walk through the Overview screen specifically.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Top of the page is a summary strip, four key metrics, active users, conversion rate, average funnel completion time, and open alerts count. Below that is a chart area that defaults to the account's most viewed funnel.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: I like defaulting to most viewed funnel instead of a generic chart, that's a nice touch.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: How do we determine most viewed, is that tracked already?

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: We'd need a small addition, tracking which funnel view gets opened most per account. Kenji, is that something we already log anywhere?

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: We log page views generally but not funnel specific view counts, that would need a new event and a small aggregation query. Probably two or three days of work.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Good to know, I'll note that as a dependency.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Let's keep going, what's next on the screen?

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Below the chart is an activity feed, recent alerts fired, recent exports, recent cohort saves once that ships. It's meant to feel a bit more alive than the current static dashboard.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: I really like that, it reinforces that things are happening in the product even if you're not actively poking around.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: Activity feed sounds like it needs a new table or at least a unified event log across alerts, exports, and cohorts. Right now those live in three separate tables with different schemas.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Is that a big lift?

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: Not huge, but not trivial either, I'd estimate about a week to build a unified activity log table and backfill recent history.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Let's flag that as a dependency for phase one then, since the activity feed is kind of the centerpiece of the new Overview screen.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Agreed, noting that.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Moving on, what about the Funnels section itself?

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Mostly the same functionally, but visually cleaner, we reduced the number of clicks to build a new funnel from five steps to three by combining the event picker and the filter picker into one screen.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: That's a nice simplification, should be low risk from an engineering side, mostly frontend.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: Agreed, that one doesn't touch backend much at all.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Good. Now, the part I actually want the most feedback on, color and visual hierarchy. We moved away from the blue and gray palette to a slightly warmer palette, more contrast between primary actions and secondary ones.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Can you pull up the actual mockup? I want to see the contrast in practice, not just hear about it.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Sharing screen now. So primary buttons are this deep teal, secondary actions are outlined only, and destructive actions like deleting a saved funnel are this muted red, not the bright red we used before.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: The muted red is a good call, the old bright red felt alarming even for minor actions.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: I like the teal, it's distinct without being loud. One thing though, is there enough contrast for accessibility? We had a complaint last year about low contrast text on the settings page.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Good catch, I ran this through a contrast checker, everything's at least four point five to one, which meets WCAG AA for normal text. I can double check the smaller label text specifically though.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Appreciate that, let's not ship something we have to immediately patch.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: From a technical standpoint, are we introducing new design tokens or reusing the existing color variables?

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: New tokens, but I tried to keep the naming consistent with what already exists so it's not a total rewrite of the theme file.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: That helps a lot, appreciate you thinking about that.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Let's talk timeline and phasing since this is a lot of surface area to ship at once.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: I'd suggest phase one is just Overview and the new navigation structure, phase two is Funnels and Cohorts visual updates, phase three is Alerts and Settings.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: That phasing makes sense, Overview and navigation are the highest visibility changes anyway.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Kenji, rough gut check on phase one engineering time given the activity log dependency?

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: With the unified activity log and the funnel view tracking, I'd guess two and a half to three weeks for phase one including QA.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: That's workable, especially since it overlaps with some downtime after the funnel builder fix wraps.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: One more thing before we close, have we user tested any of this yet, even informally?

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: I did five quick sessions last week with existing customers, four out of five preferred the new navigation immediately, the fifth wanted to keep Reports as its own tab specifically.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Four out of five is a good signal, I'm comfortable moving forward given that.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: What did the fifth person say specifically about keeping Reports separate? Curious if that's a pattern worth designing around or just one person's preference.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: They mentioned using Reports as a bookmark, going straight there every morning without looking at anything else. It's a valid workflow, just not the majority one based on the usage data.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Could we solve that with a pinned or default landing page setting instead of keeping the whole tab structure around it?

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: That's actually a nice idea, a small preference to set your default landing view within Overview. I'll sketch that as an option for phase one.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: That should be a small addition, just a user preference field, not a structural change.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Good, that addresses the one dissenting data point without adding real engineering cost. Agreed, let's move to engineering scoping. I'll have Kenji write up a proper estimate doc by early next week.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: I can have that by Wednesday.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: I'll finalize the phase one mockups with the accessibility fixes by Friday so engineering has a clean handoff.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Great, sounds like a solid session. Thanks Elena, this is a big step up from the current dashboard.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Thanks everyone, appreciate the thorough feedback.

summary.overview:
Elena presented the dashboard redesign ahead of engineering estimation, replacing the twelve-item sidebar with five top-level sections (Overview, Funnels, Cohorts, Alerts, Settings) and folding Reports into Overview based on usage data. The new Overview screen introduces a summary metrics strip, a chart defaulting to the account's most-viewed funnel, and an activity feed unifying alerts, exports, and cohort saves, the last of which requires Kenji to build a new unified activity log table, estimated at about a week.

The team reviewed a warmer color palette with a deep teal primary action color and muted red for destructive actions, replacing the previous bright red. Priya raised an accessibility concern from a past complaint about low contrast text; Elena confirmed WCAG AA compliance for body text via a contrast checker and will double check smaller label text before final handoff. Five informal user test sessions showed four of five participants preferring the new navigation.

The redesign will ship in three phases, starting with Overview and navigation, estimated at two and a half to three weeks of engineering time including the activity log dependency. Kenji will deliver a full estimate doc by Wednesday and Elena will finalize phase one mockups with accessibility fixes by Friday.
